title: REANA - Outpatient Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing via App in Adolescents with Anorexia Nervosa
summary: Anorexia nervosa is a serious eating disorder that affects an increasing number of adolescents and can have severe consequences for health. Despite existing treatment options, there are still many challenges in the therapy of adolescents with anorexia. This study therefore tests a new digital app designed to support adolescents as part of a specialized therapy. This therapy is called EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing), which uses eye movements to help process distressing thoughts and anxieties. The aim of the study is to examine whether the app can be used in the daily lives of adolescents, whether it helps reduce anxieties related to eating, and how the adolescents perceive the app overall. The study aims to show whether digital tools can provide helpful support in the treatment of anorexia.

interventions.name: Intervention group (n = 10), EMDR app use 2–3 times per week for 6 weeks, with session durations of 20–60 minutes.﻿
Waitlist control group (n = 10), 6 weeks without EMDR app use, receiving treatment as usual (TAU).﻿

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female adolescents aged 13 to 17 years
Confirmed diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (F50.0, F50.1)
Outpatient treatment at the eating disorder outpatient clinic at LWL University Hospital Hamm
Informed consent of the participant and legal guardians
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality
Use of opioids or sedatives
Dependence or abuse of medication, alcohol, or drugs
Severe cognitive impairment
Insufficient knowledge of German language
